skill.name: godot-gdscript-patterns
skill.description: Apply Godot 4 GDScript patterns for signals, scenes, state machines, save systems, components, and performance.
skill.summary: Use proven Godot 4 GDScript patterns to build maintainable game systems.
skill.author: wshobson

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, Godot resource-loading APIs, documentation URLs, and local node-path usage. One confirmed issue remains: the save-system example hardcodes an encryption key placeholder and passes it to encrypted file storage. No prompt injection text was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Hardcoded encryption key in save-system example
remediation.suggestion: Replace the hardcoded ENCRYPTION_KEY example with guidance to provide a project-specific secret outside source control. Add a warning that placeholder keys must not be shipped.

content.value_statement: Godot projects often become hard to maintain as scenes, signals, and saves expand. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical GDScript patterns for maintainable game systems.
actual_capabilities: Shows state machine patterns for player and gameplay behavior.
Explains autoload managers and global signal buses for shared game state.
Demonstrates resource-based data, component systems, and object pooling.
Provides scene loading and transition patterns for Godot projects.
Covers save and load structures with encrypted file storage examples.
Lists performance tips for caching, typing, pooling, and process control.
limitations: The skill is documentation only and does not include runnable project files.
Examples require adaptation to each game scene tree and input map.
The save-system example includes a hardcoded placeholder key that must be replaced.
The guidance focuses on Godot 4 and may not fit older Godot versions.

use_cases.title: Plan a Player State System
use_cases.description: Design movement, attack, jump, and idle states with clear transition responsibilities.

use_cases.title: Organize Shared Game Managers
use_cases.description: Structure autoloads, signal buses, scene loading, and save managers without tight coupling.

use_cases.title: Review Godot Performance Patterns
use_cases.description: Check code for repeated node lookups, allocation hot spots, and missed pooling opportunities.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how I should use signals, scenes, and resources in a small Godot 4 project. Keep the explanation practical.

prompt_templates.title: Design a State Machine
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Godot 4 GDScript state machine for a player with idle, move, jump, attack, and hurt states.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Game Systems
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Godot game architecture and suggest where to use autoloads, components, resources, and object pools.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Performance and Saves
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my Godot 4 GDScript systems for performance issues, save-system risks, and scene loading problems.

output_examples.input: I need a clean structure for player behavior in Godot 4.
output: A state machine layout with separate idle, move, jump, attack, and hurt responsibilities.
A transition plan that keeps input handling, physics updates, and animation calls organized.
Notes on when signals should replace direct node references.

output_examples.input: My project has many enemies and bullets, and performance drops during combat.
output: An object pooling approach for frequently spawned scenes.
A component split for health, hitboxes, and hurtboxes.
A checklist for cached references, static typing, and reduced allocations.

output_examples.input: I want to add save files and scene transitions.
output: A save manager responsibility map for storing progress and loading data safely.
A scene manager flow for progress signals, transitions, and asynchronous loading.
A warning to avoid shipping hardcoded encryption keys.

best_practices: Adapt each pattern to your scene tree instead of copying it unchanged.
Use signals and resources to reduce tight coupling between gameplay systems.
Replace placeholder save secrets before using encrypted storage in a real project.
anti_patterns: Do not place all gameplay logic in one global autoload.
Do not perform repeated node lookups inside hot process loops.
Do not ship save encryption with a hardcoded placeholder key.

faq.question: Which Godot version does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Godot 4.x and uses Godot 4 GDScript syntax and APIs.

faq.question: Does the skill create a complete game project?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and examples that you adapt inside your own project.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it cover state machines?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a state machine pattern with states, transitions, and input handling.

faq.question: Does it include performance guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers cached references, object pooling, static typing, and allocation reduction.

faq.question: Is the save-system example production ready?
faq.answer: Not as written. Replace the hardcoded placeholder key and adapt storage rules before release.
